subject: Renewal: Pernova - proposal to move renewal to AWS Marketplace billing
messages:
From: Sam Huang <sam.huang@pernova.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation and billing options

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the heads up — we have Pernova's annual renewal coming up on 12/10. Procurement asked whether we can move the contract to the AWS Marketplace to streamline invoicing and leverage our centralized purchasing. They also called out two constraints: (1) we need line-item visibility by environment (dev/stage/prod) on the invoice, and (2) any change can't break our existing SSO/SCIM provisioning flow.

Can Redwood support a Marketplace-based renewal that preserves our entitlement mapping and produces consolidated invoices for our finance team? If so, please send a short checklist of what you need from us and an expected timeline — procurement wants to lock this down before Thanksgiving.

Appreciate it,
Sam Huang
VP, IT Procurement
Pernova Analytics

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation and billing options

Sam — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: yes, we can migrate Pernova's renewal to AWS Marketplace and preserve entitlement mapping; there are a few ops items we'll need to coordinate. I'll outline below and mark owners.

Summary of ask (owners in parentheses):
- Confirm SKU-to-environment mapping + current seat counts (Pernova)
- Decide whether Pernova wants consolidated monthly invoices or one annual Marketplace charge (Pernova, Ben)
- Verify SCIM/SSO service account access for provisioning changes during cutover (Pernova + Karithk)
- Legal: minimal amendment vs. new Marketplace contract (Marissa + Legal)

Timeline: if we get mapping + procurement approval by 11/22, we can complete Marketplace enrollment and cutover in the first week of December and keep the 12/10 renewal effective date.

I'll attach a one-page doc that explains trade-offs (billing cadence, refunds, seat adjustments).

Grace O'Connor
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Renewal conversation and billing options

Looping in internal ops + finance: procurement is keen on Marketplace because their CFO wants a single procurement channel. Two commercial points to resolve before we commit:

1) Pricing/credits: Pernova is pushing for a 15% renewal credit if we agree to move to Marketplace (they cite administrative savings). Are we comfortable with a Marketplace-eligible credit or should we hold firm on published rates? (Ben)
2) Entitlement model: if we switch to the standard marketplace SKU mapping, we'll need to ensure our usage metering aligns with Pernova's internal cost centers — Karithik can run the entitlement mapping exercise and confirm if any product-level changes are required. (Karthik)
3) Invoicing: if Pernova wants monthly consolidated invoices but Marketplace only supports monthly billing at the partner level, we need to confirm that AWS can produce the per-environment line items they want. I'll sync with our marketplace ops contact, but Ben, can you confirm whether we can provide a CSV export to Pernova finance as a stop-gap?

Suggested next steps for this thread:
- Ben: confirm what finance can provide (CSV exports, interim invoices) by EOD Wed 11/17
- Karthik: schedule a 30-min entitlement mapping call with Pernova's SREs by 11/18
- Grace/Marissa: draft the minimal amendment language (marketplace enrollment + billing cadence) and share redline by 11/19

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation and billing options

Thanks Marissa — that plan looks good. A couple quick clarifications from procurement:

- A 15% administrative credit sounds reasonable if it can be applied up front in our renewal year rather than as a rebate. We don't want multi-step reconciliation.
- For SCIM/SSO: we can provision a temporary ops account with the right scope during cutover. I'll share access details in a secure ticket once you confirm the cutover window.
- We will need a DocuSign amendment that references the Marketplace listing and states that Redwood will accept Marketplace terms for billing. If you can draft that and route to our procurement lead (Maya), we can turn it within 48 hours.

Thanks — Sam
